claims.text: A Cu-containing high-entropy alloy, such as a CoCrFeNiCu-type alloy, can be used as a coating on a Cu matrix.
Depositing the Cu-containing HEA onto Cu can form a compositionally graded interfacial layer.
The graded interfacial layer ensures strong adhesion between the HEA coating and Cu substrate.
The Cu-containing HEA coating imparts enhanced wear resistance to the Cu substrate.
The initial Cu substrate has a native oxide and a typical grain structure.
A Cu-containing HEA thin film can be deposited onto Cu by sputtering or thermal spraying.
Controlled thermal and atmospheric deposition conditions can promote limited interdiffusion while avoiding detrimental phases.
Optimizing deposition temperature and rate can avoid excessive oxide formation and brittle intermetallics.
Limited interdiffusion between the Cu substrate and HEA produces a compositionally graded interface.
The compositionally graded interface reduces interfacial stresses.
The HEA has inherently high wear resistance.
Including Cu in the HEA creates chemical similarity with the Cu substrate that facilitates strong interfacial bonding.
The graded layer minimizes thermal-mismatch and lattice-mismatch stresses.
Reducing mismatch stresses enhances coating adhesion and mechanical durability during wear.
A Cu substrate coated with the Cu-containing HEA will have a lower wear rate than uncoated Cu.
A Cu substrate coated with the Cu-containing HEA will have a higher scratch-test critical load than uncoated Cu.
Excessive interdiffusion can produce brittle intermetallic compounds and compromise adhesion and wear performance.
Inadequately controlled surface oxides can compromise adhesion and wear improvements.
Thermal-expansion mismatch beyond the graded interface may limit performance under extreme conditions.
